content.overview: Article 152 provides that in Part VI (The States), unless the context otherwise requires, the expression ‘State’ does not include the State of Jammu and Kashmir (historical text; post-reorganisation and Article 370 changes, the territorial application of Part VI follows the current constitutional position on States and Union territories as applicable).
content.glance: In Part VI, ‘State’ is defined for the purposes of the Part (historical exclusion of J&K; apply current constitutional map of States).
content.study:
Article 152 is the definition clause for Part VI. Historically it excluded Jammu and Kashmir from the expression ‘State’ in this Part. After the constitutional changes relating to J&K and the reorganisation into Union territories, the operative map of States and UTs is governed by the current text of the Constitution and related orders. For examination purposes, state that Part VI governs the States and that Article 152 is the Part-specific definition provision.

Examination: Part VI definition; historical J&K exclusion; use current State/UT structure in application.

sections.heading: Key point
sections.body: Definition clause for Part VI (The States). Historical text excluded J&K; apply the current constitutional position on States and Union territories.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does Article 152 provide?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 152 is the definition provision for Part VI (The States). In its historical form it provided that, unless the context otherwise requires, ‘State’ in that Part did not include the State of Jammu and Kashmir. The current application of Part VI follows the Constitution as amended and the present organisation of States and Union territories.
